text:
kevin: Heads-up: canary pool in eu-west is showing a new failure pattern after the toolkit12 rollout. Pods hit node-level LD_PRELOAD/runtime errors and NCCL net connect failures.

eva: Seen it too. A small subset of nodes report libstdc++ mismatch when containers built with gcc11 run against host-provided CUDA12 libs. Example: 
```
libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.30' not found (required by /usr/local/cuda-12.0/lib64/libcudart.so)
```

infra-bot: Alert created: INFRA-3221 - toolkit12 canary: libstdc++ ABI mismatch on 18 nodes.

maggie: Also seeing NCCL noise on the same hosts: 
```
NCCL WARN NET/IB : Error querying device attributes - errno 22
NCCL WARN Call to connect failed : Transport endpoint is not connected
```

rohan: Are these nodes running the new driver or old? Kernel module logs show some tainting signs. From dmesg: `nvidia: module verification failed: signature and taints` then teardown of uvm.

kevin: Host drivers were bumped last week (525->535) to match CUDA12. But a subset of older instances still have mixed-toolchain images. The container rebuilds we pushed yesterday replaced system-lib bundles with toolchain-shared variants to reduce image size — that likely exposed the ABI mismatch.

sre-oncall: Immediate impact: a small fraction of inference pods rerouted to on-demand fallback pool, which spiked our Dedicated burst usage by ~12% for 2h and added ~4k USD last billing window. We should reconcile cost vs availability before broader rollout.

eva: Proposed actions: 
- Pause further toolkit12 expansion to other regions.
- Create a scheduler affinity that prefers nodes with a verified runtime-toolchain tag.
- Kick off a fast image rebuild that vendors the expected libstdc++ for CUDA12 containers.

maggie: Also suggests we add an automatic fallback policy in the router: when NCCL connect fails, fall back to intra-region CPU-optimized replicas for short calls (< 200ms) to avoid cross-region hops. That would reduce cross-region egress and cost.

luis: I can prepare a minimized rebuild pipeline that injects a static libstdc++ into the CUDA CLI images and push to canary. ETA 3–4h.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout (image: rwd/toolkit12-runtime:v20260318-canary2) started to eu-west-canary (12 nodes). Tracking health checks.

rohan: Quick diagnostic: marking 6 of the affected nodes with label `toolkit12-raw=false` so scheduler avoids them. Putting them into maintenance for a patch.

kevin: Long-term we need a preflight probe that validates container/toolkit ABI combos on node provision and a stricter image provenance guard so we don't ship trimmed libstdc++ variants to CUDA-dependent images.

sre-oncall: I'll file a postmortem ticket and include cost delta. Short-term runbook: 
1) Pause rollout in other regions (done).
2) Route new inference traffic away from flagged nodes (rohan done).
3) Push luis's static-lib rebuild to canary and monitor for 1h.
4) If stable, promote and gradually ramp with autoscale caps to limit cost.

eva: Also recommend adding a kernel-module version check in node-autoprovision: if host driver != expected-driver-for-toolkit, mark node as ineligible for toolkit12 workloads. Avoids partial upgrades.

maggie: For transparency, logging the NCCL/network errors to a dedicated metric so we can track regressions post-fix.

kevin: Thanks all. Keep the thread updated. If the canary succeeds, we still throttle the regional rollout and coordinate driver upgrade windows with provisioning to avoid half-upgraded pools. :thumbsup:
